name: Mandala Bloom
description: Radial expansion architecture mapping octahedral symmetry to 8 petals with topological attention. Each petal corresponds to an O_h vertex state, with Golden Ratio spacing between bloom layers. Topological protection through winding number invariants preserves charge under deformation. Vortex memory anchors position at write-time.

core_attributes.pattern: radial expansion, 8-petal octahedral mapping, topological attention, vortex memory

scope.definition: Fraction of natural biological radial structures (flowers, sea anemones, jellyfish, starfish) exhibiting 4- or 8-fold versus other symmetry orders — testing octahedral symmetry prevalence in nature.

evidence.source: Coxeter (1961) 'Introduction to Geometry', Wiley; Weyl (1952) 'Symmetry', Princeton UP — symmetry in nature.
cross_domain_examples: flowering plants: 3, 4, 5-fold symmetry dominant — 4-fold common in Brassicaceae, 5-fold in Rosaceae
echinoderms: 5-fold symmetry exclusively — evolutionary constraint from ancestral body plan
diatoms: radial symmetry from 3 to 40+ folds — unique diversity of biological symmetry orders

scope.falsifiability: If systematic survey finds 4-fold and 8-fold symmetry no more common than other symmetry orders in natural biological structures, octahedral symmetry is not a dominant natural pattern.
scope.measurement_limits: Symmetry order is phylogenetically constrained — different lineages show different symmetry defaults. 5-fold symmetry is unusual in physics but dominant in biology. 4- and 8-fold symmetry are common in crystals.
